source_text: ἐρῶ– τὸ μέγα καὶ μόνον μέγα μικρῷ συμβάλλων–ὡς ἅμα τε ἥλιος, ἅμα ἐξ ἡλίου φύσεως καὶ ἐξ ὅλου τοῦ δίσκου ἀμερίστως καὶ ἀδιαστάτως καὶ ἰσομέτρως ὅλον τὸ φῶς συνεκφαίνεται καὶ συνενεργεῖ καὶ συμπαρέχει τὴν θέρμην τοῖς αἰσθήσεως δεκτικοῖς. καὶ τῆς τοῦ προέντος οὐσίας τὸ ἀμέσως καὶ οὐχ ὕστερον προχεόμενον καὶ συμπροϊὸν καὶ συνυφιστάμενον φῶς ὅλην ἐν ἑαυτῷ διεκφαίνει τὴν ποιότητα. 15.36 Εἰ δέ, πρὸς τὸ εἶκον ἐκείνοις, «ἦν ὅτε οὐκ ἦν» τὸ ἀπαύγασμα, ποῦ ἡ ἀπαυγάζουσα αὐτὸ ὑπόστασις τοῦ φωτός; συνδιολισθήσει γάρ που πάντως ἐκείνῳ τοῦτο. καὶ μὴν καὶ ∆ανιὴλ προφητεύων εἶπεν· «καὶ φῶς μετ' αὐτοῦ ἦν» ἀντὶ τοῦ «ὁ υἱὸς μετὰ τοῦ πατρός». 15.37 Τοῦτο γὰρ μάλιστα δείκνυσιν τὸ ἀσυνείκαστον καὶ μέγα τῆς θεότητος, ὅτι συνάναρχον αὐτοῦ καὶ σύναρχον ὁμοῦ δὲ καὶ τέλειον καὶ ἀπαράλλακτον ἀπαθῶς ἐγέννησεν ὁ πατήρ. 15.38 κτίσματος γὰρ ἴδιον καὶ οὐ κτίστου, τρεπτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἀτρέπτου, ὑπὸ κρίσιν καὶ οὐ κριτοῦ, ζωοποιουμένου καὶ οὐ ζωοποιοῦντος, ὑπὸ ἁμαρτίαν καὶ οὐ θεοῦ τὸ μὴ οὕτως γεννῆσαι καὶ γεννηθῆναι. 15.39 εἰ γὰρ αὐτός, οὔπω ἐνεργείας ἄλλης οὐδεμιᾶς γενομένης, «ἐποίησεν τοὺς αἰῶνας», οἱ ἐκ τῶν χρόνων ἀποτελοῦνται, καὶ τοῖς πᾶσιν ἀρχὴν ἐπέθηκεν, οὐδὲν δὲ πρὸ τῶν χρόνων καὶ αἰώνων νοεῖσθαι δύναται εἰ μὴ ἡ ἀκατάληπτος καὶ ἀληθῶς μόνη πρωτίστη καὶ πρωτουργὸς φύσις ἡ μόνως οὖσα ἄναρχος καὶ αἰώνιος καὶ 9 ὕφεσιν πρὸς ἑτέραν οὐκ ἔχουσα, πῶς οὐκ ἀνάρχως ἐκ τῆς ὑποστάσεως γεννηθῆναι πιστεύεται τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ οὐκ ἐκ τῆς ἐνεργείας; 15.40 χρόνου γὰρ οὐ διορίζοντος οὐκ ἔστιν πρότερον καὶ ὕστερον, ἀλλ' ὁ μὴ ὢν ὑπὸ χρόνον ἄναρχός ἐστιν, ὁ δὲ ἄναρχος ἄκτιστος. 15.41 ὥσπερ γὰρ οὐκ ἔστι χρόνος ἀγένητος, οὕτως οὐδὲ κτίσις ἄχρονος, ἀλλ' ἔχει μέτρον τὸν χρόνον· σὺν αὐτῇ γὰρ καὶ ὁ χρόνος γέγονεν. καὶ εἰκότως πάντα μὲν ἀπὸ τοῦ δημιουργοῦ μετρεῖται ὡς δεύτερα, αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπ' οὐδενός, ἐπειδὴ ἄναρχος καὶ φύσει θεός. 15.42 Τὰ δὲ ἴσα θεωρεῖται καὶ περὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος. οὐ γὰρ γέγραπταί ποτε «ἐξεπορεύθη», ἀλλ' «ἐκπορεύεται». πῶς δὲ αὐτὴ ἡ ζωὴ ζωοποιεῖται ἢ τὸ ἀληθινὸν φῶς φωτίζεται; 15.43 Ἦν δὲ ἄρα τό τε θεῖον φῶς καί «ζωὴ αἰώνιος» ἀεί, καὶ αὐτὸς ἑαυτὸν λέγει ὁ ἀψευδὴς καὶ μέγας θεός. 15.44 οὐ μὴ ἦν ὅτε «ἀπαύγασμα δόξης καὶ χαρακτῆρα ὑποστάσεως καὶ εἰκόνα ἀγαθότητος καὶ δύναμιν καὶ σοφίαν καὶ δικαιοσύνην θεοῦ» ἃ ὑπάρχειν τὸν αὐτὸν μονογενῆ Παῦλος μαρτυρεῖ οὐκ εἶχεν ὁ πατήρ, ἀλλ', ὃ μὴ προσῆκεν εἰπεῖν, ὕστερον ὁτιοῦν προσέλαβεν. 15.45 εἰ δὲ εἶχεν, ἦν ἀεὶ ὁ ταῦτα ὢν μονογενής. 15.46 οὔτε γὰρ ὁ ταῦτα ὢν ἐκτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ οὔτε ὁ θεὸς χωρὶς τοῦ ὄντος αὐτοῦ ταῦτά ποτε νοηθῆναι δύναται. ταῦτα δὲ ὑπάρχει ὁ μονογενής, οὐ καθάπερ ἕξις ἢ ἐπιτηδειότης, ἀλλ' οὐσιωδῶς, καθὰ προείρηται. 15.47 Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀρχῇ τῆς κοσμογονίας τὰ πρῶτα δένδρα σὺν τοῖς ἐξ αὐτῶν καρποῖς συνυπέστη–καὶ παράδοξον οὐδέν, εἰ σὺν τῇ ῥίζῃ ὁ καρπὸς συνανέτειλεν–, πῶς ἀμήχανον κατ' ἀρχὰς τὸν εὐμήχανον πατέρα μὴ ἔγκαρπον γεγενῆσθαι τοῦ ἰδίου υἱοῦ καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ τῆς δόξης τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ συνεκλάμψαι τὸ ἀπαύγασμα; 15.48 καθὰ οὖν αὐτοῦ ἡ τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως κάτω γέννησις ἑτέρᾳ γεννήσει οὐ συγκρίνεται–ἐκ παρθένου γὰρ ἄρευστος, ἀπήμαντος, ὅπερ ἡ φύσις ἡμῶν οὐκ ἔχει–, οὕτω καὶ ἡ ἄνω γέννησις ἀκατάληπτος ὑπὲρ τὸ πλέον καὶ πᾶσαν ἐξαλλάττουσα γέννησιν ὑπάρχει. καὶ οὔτε ἀπιστεῖν χρὴ οὔτε μὴν ζητεῖν ἢ ἐξηγεῖσθαι τὸν τρόπον ἡμῖν ἀσφαλὲς τοῖς εἰπεῖν μὴ δυναμένοις, πῶς παρθένος ἔτεκεν μείνασα παρθένος μήτε δὲ τὴν ἰδίαν ἡμῶν γέννησιν ἐπισταμένοις. 15.49 ὅπου γε καὶ τὴν καθ' ἡμᾶς εἰ ἐγινώσκομεν, οὐ πάντως καὶ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἥτις καὶ ταῖς ἐπουρανίοις δυνάμεσιν ἀκατάληπτος οὖσα τυγχάνει. 15.50 ∆ιὸ σὺν ἐκπλήξει ὁ προφήτης φησὶν περὶ μὲν τῆς κάτω γεννήσεως· «καὶ ἄνθρωπός ἐστιν καὶ τίς
pass_a_gloss: [15.35 continued, from the previous section] I will say (comparing the great and alone great to a small thing) that as at once there is a sun, at once out of the nature of the sun and out of the whole disk, undividedly and without interval and in equal measure, the whole light is shown forth together and works together and furnishes together the heat to the things receptive of sense-perception. And the light, being poured forth immediately and not later and going forth together and subsisting together, displays through in itself the whole quality of the substance of the one that sent it forth. 15.36 But if, according to what seems good to those men, 'there was when there was not' the radiance, where is the hypostasis of the light that radiates it? For this one will surely somehow slip away together with that one. And truly also Daniel, prophesying, said: 'and light was with him', in place of 'the Son with the Father'. 15.37 For this most of all shows the not-to-be-conjectured and great [quality] of the Godhead, that the Father begot, impassibly, one co-without-beginning with him and co-ruling, and at the same time also perfect and unvarying [from him]. 15.38 For the not thus begetting and being begotten is proper to a creature and not to a creator, to a changeable one and not to an unchangeable one, to one under judgment and not to a judge, to one being made alive and not to one making alive, to one under sin and not to God. 15.39 For if he himself, when as yet no other activity at all had come about, 'made the ages', which are brought to completion out of the times, and laid a beginning upon all things, and nothing can be thought before the times and ages except the incomprehensible and truly sole, very first and first-working nature, the one solely being without beginning and eternal and having no lowering toward another, how is he not believed to have been begotten beginninglessly out of the hypostasis of the Father and not out of the activity? 15.40 For with time not marking off there is not earlier and later, but the one not being under time is beginningless, and the beginningless one is uncreated. 15.41 For just as there is not an unoriginated time, so neither a timeless creation, but it has time as a measure; for together with it time also has come to be. And reasonably all things are measured from the craftsman as second things, but he himself by none, since he is beginningless and God by nature. 15.42 And the equal things are beheld concerning the Holy Spirit also. For it has not been written anywhere 'he proceeded', but 'he proceeds'. And how is the life itself made alive, or the true light lit up? 15.43 So then both the divine light and 'eternal life' was always, and the unlying and great God himself speaks of himself [so]. 15.44 By no means was there [a time] when the Father did not have 'radiance of glory and stamp of hypostasis and image of goodness and power and wisdom and righteousness of God', which Paul bears witness that the same only-begotten is, but, what it was not fitting to say, took on anything whatever afterward. 15.45 But if he had [them], the only-begotten, the one being these things, was always. 15.46 For neither can the one being these things ever be thought outside God, nor God apart from the one being these things of his. And the only-begotten is these things, not like a holding or a fitness, but substantially, according as was said before. 15.47 And if also at the beginning of the world's genesis the first trees came to subsist together with the fruits out of them (and nothing contrary to expectation, if the fruit rose up together with the root), how [is it] without means that at the start the well-resourced Father did not become fruit-bearing with his own Son, and straightway the radiance shone out together from the glory of his hypostasis? 15.48 According as, then, his below-birth of the becoming-man is not compared with another birth (for out of a virgin, flux-free, unharmed, which our nature does not have), so also the above-birth is incomprehensible beyond the more and exceeding every birth. And neither must one disbelieve, nor indeed [is it] safe for us to seek or to expound the manner, for us who are not able to say how a virgin bore having remained a virgin, and who do not understand our own birth either. 15.49 Seeing that, even if we knew the [birth] according to us, [we would] not at all [know] also that of God, which indeed happens to be incomprehensible even to the heavenly powers. 15.50 On which account with astonishment the prophet says concerning the below-birth: 'and he is a man, and who [breaks off; continued in the next section]
pass_b_english: … I will say, comparing the great, the only truly great, with something small: as soon as there is a sun, at that same moment the whole light shines forth with it from the sun’s nature and from the whole disk, undivided, without interval and in equal measure; it works together with the sun and together with it gives warmth to everything that can receive sensation. And the light that is poured out at once and not later, that goes forth with its source and subsists with it, displays in itself the whole quality of the substance that sent it forth.

But if, as those people would have it, “there was when the radiance was not,” where is the hypostasis of the light that sends that radiance out? It must surely slip away together with the radiance. And indeed Daniel too said in prophecy, “And light was with him” (Daniel 2:22), meaning “the Son was with the Father.”

For this above all shows how great the Godhead is, and how far beyond all guessing: the Father begot, without passion, one who is without beginning together with him and shares his rule, and who is at the same time perfect and his exact likeness. Not to beget and be begotten in this way belongs to a creature and not to the Creator, to what is changeable and not to the unchangeable, to what is under judgment and not to the Judge, to what is given life and not to the giver of life, to what is under sin and not to God.

For if he himself, before any other activity at all had taken place, “made the ages” (Hebrews 1:2), which are made up of times, and set a beginning to all things; and if nothing can be conceived before times and ages except the incomprehensible nature, truly the only one, the first of all and the first at work, which alone is without beginning and eternal and stands lower than no other: how can he not be believed to have been begotten without beginning from the Father’s hypostasis, and not from his activity? Where time sets no bounds, there is no earlier and later. What is not under time is without beginning, and what is without beginning is uncreated. Just as there is no time that did not come into being, so there is no creation without time: creation has time as its measure, for time came into being together with it. And fittingly all things are measured from the Maker as coming second, but he himself is measured by nothing, since he is without beginning and God by nature.

The same holds for the Holy Spirit. For Scripture nowhere says “he proceeded,” but “he proceeds” (John 15:26). And how can life itself be given life, or the true light be enlightened? So the divine light and “eternal life” (1 John 5:20) always was, and that is what the truthful and great God calls himself.

There was certainly never a time when the Father did not have “the radiance of glory and the stamp of the hypostasis and the image of goodness and the power and wisdom and righteousness of God” (Hebrews 1:3; Wisdom of Solomon 7:26; 1 Corinthians 1:24; 1 Corinthians 1:30), which Paul testifies that the same Only-begotten is, and then (what it is not fitting even to say) took on any of these later. But if he had them, then the Only-begotten, who is these things, always was. For neither can the one who is these things ever be conceived outside God, nor God without the one who is these things for him. And the Only-begotten is these things not as a state or an aptitude, but in his very being, as was said before.

And if at the beginning of the world’s making the first trees came into being together with their fruit (and there is nothing strange in the fruit springing up together with the root), how could the Father, who lacks no resource, have been so without resource as not to be fruitful with his own Son from the beginning, and the radiance not to shine forth at once from the glory of his hypostasis?

So then, just as his birth below, the birth of his becoming man, cannot be compared with any other birth (for it was from a virgin, without flux and without injury, which our nature does not have), so too his birth above is incomprehensible, and still more so, and differs from every other birth. We must not disbelieve it; nor is it safe for us to search out or explain the manner, since we cannot say how a virgin gave birth and remained a virgin, and we do not even understand our own birth. Even if we knew ours, we would by no means know God’s as well, for it is incomprehensible even to the heavenly powers.
Therefore the prophet says in amazement about the birth below: “And he is a man, and who …”

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, broken and numbered
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed edition numbers 15.36-15.50 in the reading text; broke 15.41 off at 'since...' and turned the rest into a fragment paragraph ('Indeed, the God who is without beginning and is by nature.'); ended with a stray paragraph 'The text ends abruptly mid-sentence.'; read ἀσυνείκαστον (beyond conjecture) as 'unmixed', σύναρχον as 'co-existing' and the adverb ἀπαθῶς as 'impassible' of the Son; made 15.38 'under sin and not of God' a garble; read ὕφεσιν (inferiority) as 'ties to another' and doubled that clause; read ζωοποιεῖται (is given life) as 'made life-giving'; turned 15.44 upside down; read ἄρευστος, ἀπήμαντος as 'incomparable, being without a man' and ἐξαλλάττουσα as 'transforming all'; garbled 15.49; and used a bracket filler '[words]'. References: John 1:4 for “eternal life” replaced by 1 John 5:20 (the quoted phrase); Daniel 2:22 and Hebrews 1:2 kept; Hebrews 1:3 kept and Wisdom of Solomon 7:26, 1 Corinthians 1:24 and 1:30 added for the four parts of the list; John 15:26 added for “he proceeds”.

choices.term: ἐρῶ– τὸ μέγα καὶ μόνον μέγα μικρῷ συμβάλλων
choices.english: … I will say, comparing the great, the only truly great, with something small
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence: 15.35 (previous section) begins the period ('so that the incomparable may be shown by comparison… I will say'). Only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.

choices.english: as soon as there is a sun, at that same moment …
choices.why: The paired ἅμα makes the light simultaneous with the sun: Didymus' image for a begetting without interval.

choices.term: τῆς τοῦ προέντος οὐσίας … ὅλην … τὴν ποιότητα
choices.english: the whole quality of the substance that sent it forth
choices.why: The genitive is taken with ποιότητα (the light shows the source's whole quality), not with προχεόμενον.

choices.english: as those people would have it
choices.why: εἶκον (what seems fitting) with the dative of the opponents: the Arian slogan is their view, not his.

choices.english: It must surely slip away together with the radiance
choices.why: τοῦτο is the hypostasis of the light, ἐκείνῳ the radiance: if the radiance once was not, its source vanishes with it. Named in English so the referents are plain.

choices.english: without beginning together with him and shares his rule
choices.why: συνάναρχος already says co-eternal; σύναρχος is taken in its sense 'co-ruler' so the pair does not say the same thing twice.
ὕφεσις is a lowering or inferiority: the first nature is subordinate to none.

choices.term: πῶς ἀμήχανον … τὸν εὐμήχανον πατέρα μὴ ἔγκαρπον γεγενῆσθαι
choices.english: how could the Father, who lacks no resource, have been so without resource as not to be fruitful with his own Son
choices.why: Keeps Didymus' play on ἀμήχανος / εὐμήχανος (without means / rich in means); the rhetorical question means the Father was fruitful from the beginning.
Two adjectives of the virgin birth: no bodily flux or passion, no harm to the virgin's integrity. The old 'without a man' was not in the Greek.

choices.english: without the one who is these things for him
choices.why: αὐτοῦ marks the Son as God's own radiance, image and power; 'for him' keeps that relation without adding a claim.
The '9' inside 15.39 is a printed line number, page debris; skipped.

choices.english: “eternal life” (1 John 5:20) … is what the truthful and great God calls himself
choices.why: The quoted phrase matches 1 John 5:20 ('the true God and eternal life'), not John 1:4, which the old draft cited.
